papers.title: M5-brane source charges, Chern--Connes pairings and noncommutative compactifications
papers.abstract: We formulate a source-adapted Chern--Connes description of M5-brane magnetic charge in physically motivated noncommutative and quotient linking sectors. The starting point is the local codimension-five geometry of an M5-brane source: the magnetic charge is measured on a four-dimensional link. In the smooth local model the link is the ordinary four-sphere, and the pairing reduces to the standard flux integral of the M-theory four-form field strength. The construction is motivated by the published even-codimensional Noncommutative Foliation Invariant (NCFI for short), where Connes' transverse fundamental cyclic cocycle is paired with an even transverse-geometric \(K\)-class. For an M5-brane the relevant codimension is odd, so the required odd \(K\)-class is supplied instead by the boundary map of the source/linking extension. Noncommutative or groupoid algebras are used only when they arise from physical mechanisms: Matrix/M-theory compactification on noncommutative tori, reduction to D-branes in background \(B\)-fields, large \(C\)-field M5 limits, or quotient/orbifold source links. The result is a topological charge formula, not a derivation of the full M5-brane dynamics or of the complete M-theory action.
authors: Ioannis P. Zois

papers.title: Local Thermodynamics and R\'enyi Bounds on Black Hole Mergers
papers.abstract: R\'enyi entropy inequalities have been proposed to strengthen the area-theorem bound on mergers of thermodynamically stable black holes in Anti de Sitter (AdS) space. The stronger bounds depend on the joint initial state, whereas masses and temperatures fix only its local thermal marginals. We quantify this distinction inside the canonical two-hole description. Correlations confined to rare energy fluctuations can leave both thermal states exactly intact and drive the trace distance and mutual information to zero, yet still change the joint R\'enyi entropy at leading semiclassical order. We determine the smallest entropy compatible with a controlled approach to statistical independence, uniformly over all positive R\'enyi orders up to one. For equal Schwarzschild--AdS$_4$ holes, the resulting optimized canonical mass constraint reduces to the area bound at leading semiclassical order. The reduction concerns only the information needed to infer a bound; it does not produce a lighter attainable remnant or a dynamical instability. Stronger merger constraints therefore require control of the initial correlations beyond single black hole thermodynamics.
authors: Sudhanva Joshi, Sunil Kumar Mishra

papers.title: Horizon entropy does not by itself determine a force between black holes
papers.abstract:
The Bekenstein-Hawking law fixes the total entropy of a horizon. Membrane, holographic, and entropic-force pictures go further and follow the entropy of individual horizon elements as a configuration changes. We show that this step needs structure that the horizon geometry does not supply. Along a family of horizons labeled by $\lambda$, a relabeling of horizon points by a tangential field $v^A$ shifts the temperature-weighted entropy variation $\int T\partial_\lambda(dS)$ exactly by $-\int v^AD_AT dS$, so the horizon data determine it only when the temperature is uniform. We test this on two black holes in exact Brill-Lindquist data. At fixed physical masses each horizon area is independent of the separation through five relative orders; the low-order equilibrium force reported earlier comes from holding the bare parameters fixed instead. Weighting the redistribution of area by the nonuniform Noether-charge temperature gives a candidate repulsion equal to $(
u/8)(GM/r_{12})^3$ times the Newtonian attraction, for total mass $M$, symmetric mass ratio $
u$, and coordinate separation $r_{12}$. As a static interaction it would shift the third post-Newtonian coefficient of the circular-orbit binding energy by $5
u/48$, in conflict with general relativity. The identity resolves the conflict. Through fourth post-Newtonian order the candidate lies entirely in the dipole of the area distribution, which the uniform part of the companion's field generates as a M"obius map of the labels, and which vanishes in the area-balanced conformal frame, where the functional begins at fifth order with a coefficient that a further relabeling can still change. The marginally trapped tube of the data and the tidally deformed horizon of a post-Newtonian binary, both of which do supply an identification, transport no dipole at the order the candidate requires.
authors: Zhi-Wei Wang, Samuel L. Braunstein

papers.title: Verified Pauli-Product Measurement Compilation for Fault-Tolerant Quantum Computation
papers.abstract: Fault-tolerant quantum compilers implement gates through Pauli-product measurements and classical feedback. Verifying such a compiler requires reasoning about the quantum state and the recorded outcomes together: a correction reads an outcome, a gate's internal outcomes must be hidden from its caller, and an application's outcomes must survive optimization. We introduce QPPM, a language for Pauli-product measurement programs, with a weakest-precondition semantics over store-indexed matrix assertions, following quantum Hoare logic with classical variables. Every program terminates, so the Hoare logic is a syntactic presentation of weakest preconditions whose soundness and relative completeness are immediate. Its value is that component specifications compose. All results are mechanized in Lean. We verify lowering of Clifford+$T$ circuits to QPPM with private outcomes and supplied magic states, and an optimizer that eliminates measurements, fuses and reorders rotations, and schedules logical rounds while preserving every outcome that subsequent code can read. A compositional approximation relation bounds the effect of synthesis error on specifications and on output trace distance, and a certificate-checked pipeline selects, among synthesized circuits that meet the user's error limit, the one with the lowest certified depth bound. On QASMBench, verified fusion and scheduling reduce logical measurement depth by a median of 17.9\%, and complete source-to-QPPM allowances are certified for all 35 valid selected small-suite inputs.
authors: John Zhuoyang Ye, Jens Palsberg

papers.title: Kasner Exponents from the Bouncing Singularity
papers.abstract: The black hole singularity can be probed by the thermal boundary two-point correlator. When there is a bouncing geodesic, the boundary correlator reveals the singular behavior $G(t, \vec{x}=0) \propto (t-t_c)^{-2\Delta+b_t}$ at large $N$. We show that the additional power $b_t$ is determined by the Kasner exponents near the singularity: for planar black branes in AdS$_{d+1}$, we derive the formula $b_t=(d-1) \max \left(\frac{p_i-p_t}{1-p_t} , \frac12 \right)$, where $p_t$ and $p_i$ are the exponents of the time and spatial directions. We compare our formula with the numerical values of \v{C}eplak and Valach. It reproduces their relation for black branes with $g_{tt}g_{rr}=-1$. For $g_{tt}g_{rr}\neq-1$, where no formula had been found, our formula agrees with most of their data and fits them much better than their relation. We also give predictions for $b_t$ in theories where the Kasner exponents are known, but $b_t$ has not been computed.
authors: Hyunwoo Oh

papers.title: Matrix scattering and the black hole interior
papers.abstract: Complex-time singularities of thermal correlators carry imprints of black hole interiors. We investigate their microscopic origin in matrix quantum mechanics at high temperature, where the dynamics becomes semi-classical. We introduce a complex-time scattering kernel that encodes these singularities and makes their finite-$N$ resolution accessible to numerics. Studying both integrable and chaotic models, we find evidence for a smoothing scale $\Delta t\sim N^{-1/2}$, suggesting that the resolution is due to quantum fluctuations of D-branes. This scattering picture provides a starting point for probing the black hole interior beyond a classical geometric description.
authors: Matthew Dodelson, Henry W. Lin, Haitian Xie, Jessica Yeh

papers.title: In situ enhanced detectability of axions' responses in a microwave cavity
papers.abstract: Microwave cavities in strong magnetic fields are among the most sensitive detectors for axion dark matter detection. Its sensitivity, however, is fundamentally limited by the second order nature of axion photon energy conversion, which yields an extremely weak signal. Here we propose a feasible approach to break this limitation, by pre-exciting the target cavity mode to generate a first order power response signal in situ. The resulting signal amplitude scales linearly with the axion-photon coupling parameter, which is in sharp contrast to the quadratic scaling of conventional schemes, and is detectable via standard quadrature balanced homodyne detection system, even though its phase remains stochastic. Numerical simulations demonstrate that this pre-excited seed field can effectively suppress thermal noise, and thus the detection sensitivity of the system can approach the lower quantum noise limit. Consequently, the sensitivities predicted by the KSVZ and DFSZ models could be surpassed. This proposal might offer a pathway to a major leap in axion dark matter searches, as it is within reach of current technology.
authors: Li Gao, Suirong He, Hao Zheng, Ni Chen, Xianing Feng, Qingquan Jiang, Jin Li, L. F. Wei

papers.title: Mutual Information Across Quantum Reference Frame Perspectives
papers.abstract: In quantum information theory, standard notions typically presuppose a fixed partition of the world into subsystems, encoded in a tensor product structure of the Hilbert space. Yet, in some scenarios, the subsystem structure is not uniquely fixed. A case in point is the description of subsystems relative to different quantum reference frames (QRFs), where the tensor product structure, although fixed in a specific QRF, changes across different QRFs. Such a relativity of subsystems underlies many interesting features of QRFs, such as the relativity of entanglement, entropy, and coherence. It also raises a broader question: how do we compare the information across different subsystem perspectives, especially when the corresponding subsystem algebras overlap? Here, we propose a notion of quantum mutual information across different QRF perspectives, which captures the correlations between subsystems relative to different frames of reference. To do so, we focus on an algebraic definition of subsystems. Studying in detail the union and overlap between subsystem algebras relative to different QRFs, we find that the usual definition of mutual information in terms of the chain law overcounts the information associated to the overlap. Based on this insight, we propose a modified chain law and show that the resulting notion of mutual information satisfies subadditivity and connects naturally to other measures found in the literature [1]. Our investigations not only provide a way to quantify the relation between different QRF perspectives from an information-theoretic point of view but also sheds light on some important features of quantum information in absence of a fixed tensor product structure.
authors: Leonardo Valente, Carla Ferradini, Flaminia Giacomini, Viktoria Kabel

papers.title: Free energy fluctuations of symmetric perceptron models up to and including criticality
papers.abstract: We study the free energy fluctuations of spherical and Ising perceptron models with general even activations. These include the symmetric binary perceptron, the $U$-perceptron, and the bipartite Sherrington--Kirkpatrick model. Our main result is a Gaussian CLT for the free energy that holds both in the ``high-temperature'' interior of a second moment RS regime and on its ``critical'' boundary. At criticality, the CLT has scale $(\frac{\log N}{6})^{1/2}$, which matches the free energy fluctuations of the critical Sherrington--Kirkpatrick model and suggests this scaling is universal. The proof shows that the perceptron model's free energy fluctuations are explained, up to an additive $o(1)$ error with high probability, by those of a corresponding spherical Hopfield model, and that this relation persists even at criticality. This proof strategy builds on a critical reweighted moment method developed by the first and third authors \cite{du2026fluctuations} to identify the critical fluctuations of the SK free energy, which links these fluctuations to the spectral edge spacing of the disorder.
authors: Hang Du, Shuyang Gong, Brice Huang, Zhangsong Li

papers.title: Intertwining Defects and Fermion-Boundary Scattering from TQFT
papers.abstract: We construct conformal boundary conditions of free Dirac fermions that preserve chiral, anomaly-free symmetries, and determine the associated fermion-boundary scattering, using the TQFT/CFT framework. We apply the construction to several previously unresolved examples: higher-charge monopoles in non-chiral QED, a family of $SU(N)\times SU(N+2)$-symmetric models, the chiral QED with charges $\{1^5,3,(-2)^4\}$, and the charge-three monopole of the Standard Model. In these examples, out-going states are created by defect operators at the end of non-invertible topological lines; when such a line is non-simple, the out-going state splits into superselection sectors, and we give a formula for the branching ratios in terms of TQFT data. We also propose a general construction that adds and then gaps neutral spectators, under a technical assumption, which is potentially applicable to the 1-5-7-8-9 model.
authors: Kantaro Ohmori, Masataka Watanabe, Pengcheng Wei, Yunqin Zheng

papers.title: Strongly non-linear continuous model for wave propagation in 2D granular media: derivation and hyperbolicity analysis
papers.abstract: In this work, we develop a nonlinear continuum model for wave propagation in two-dimensional granular materials, building on key ideas from Nesterenko's work. Starting from the Hertzian contact law and neglecting contact friction, we derive an effective continuum description through homogenization, assuming spherical, monodisperse grains, local periodicity, and the Cauchy--Born hypothesis. The resulting strain-gradient model depends on both the first and second gradients of the displacement field. We analyse the hyperbolicity of the leading-order system through its eigenvalues and eigenvectors, establishing conditions for hyperbolicity within a restricted deformation domain. The model is solved using an explicit finite-volume method to investigate gravitational settling and wave propagation. We derive analytical expressions for the longitudinal and transverse wave speeds and highlight their dependence on depth. Finally, the predictions of the continuum model are compared with existing discrete-element simulations. This formulation allows several extensions, including more complex packing geometries, contact laws, and large-deformation regimes in which the contact network can evolve.
authors: Sebastiano Cominelli, R\'egis Cottereau, Sergey Gavrilyuk, Bruno Lombard, Fabien Petitpas

papers.title: FeynFacet: AI agents for analytic NLO QCD
papers.abstract: We present FeynFacet, a workflow in which artificial intelligence agents develop and execute programs for analytic next-to-leading-order (NLO) QCD calculations, with the observables and conventions specified by physicists. We use it to derive new analytic hard functions for single-inclusive transverse spin transfer in proton-proton and lepton-proton collisions. The new proton-proton results cover all partonic channels contributing to transverse spin transfer, and the new lepton-proton result is inclusive in the scattered lepton. Within FeynFacet, we use reverse unitarity to represent the on-shell delta functions in real-emission phase-space integrals as cut propagators. Dimensional shifts convert integrals containing evanescent numerators into scalar integrals in higher dimensions. Integration-by-parts identities then reduce the scalar integrals to master integrals, which are evaluated analytically. Gauge invariance, pole cancellation and renormalization-group (RG) evolution provide checks throughout the calculation. We reproduce established single-inclusive hard functions for unpolarized and double longitudinally polarized proton-proton and lepton-proton scattering, and for proton-proton scattering with two transversely polarized beams. We also reproduce the NLO matching coefficients for unpolarized quark and gluon transverse-momentum-dependent parton distributions and the associated soft functions. The new transverse spin-transfer coefficients provide perturbative inputs for extracting quark transversity through spin-dependent fragmentation, including polarized-hyperon production, Collins and dihadron asymmetries in jets, and spin-dependent one- and two-point energy correlators. We make all analytic coefficients and the associated calculation programs publicly available online.
authors: Zhong-Bo Kang, Werner Vogelsang, Congyue Zhang

papers.title: Multicriticality in the Generalized Schwinger Model
papers.abstract: We consider the generalized Schwinger model. This theory is obtained by coupling the field strength to an auxiliary scalar field $B$ and allowing generic potentials $V(B)$. We study the properties and phases of the model, focusing on the case where the potential is quartic. We investigate the model using both semiclassical and numerical methods, and find a rich phase diagram in the space of couplings. A region with unbroken charge conjugation is separated from one where the symmetry is spontaneously broken by lines of first- and second-order phase transitions. At the special point where these two lines meet, we find a fixed point in the tricritical Ising universality class. We also observe infinitely many lines of first order phase transitions ending at points of the Ising universality class.
authors: Federico Ambrosino, Bernardo Zan

papers.title: Gauge It or Break It: Lectures on Global Symmetries and the Cobordism Conjecture
papers.abstract: These lecture notes introduce the No Global Symmetries Conjecture in the context of the Swampland Program, with particular emphasis on the Cobordism Conjecture. We begin with a review of ordinary and higher-form symmetries, their realization by extended operators, and mechanisms for gauging or breaking them. We then discuss the no global symmetries principle, including evidence from black hole physics, string perturbation theory, and AdS/CFT, and its relation to other Swampland constraints. A central theme is the reformulation of symmetry constraints in topological terms: we introduce bordism groups, with special focus on spin bordism, and explain how they provide a natural framework for organizing would-be global symmetries in gravitational theories. With this at hand, we discuss the Cobordism Conjecture, which proposes that nontrivial bordism classes are eliminated by dynamical processes in quantum gravity. We conclude with examples and a discussion of dynamical aspects involving defects, boundaries, and related open questions. These notes are based on lectures delivered by Matilda Delgado at the 21st Modave Summer School on Mathematical Physics. A similar series of lectures was also presented at the KMPB School on D-branes in Physics and Mathematics.
authors: Matilda Delgado, Corinne Englert, Guillermo Mera \'Alvarez, Eduardo Velasco-Aja

papers.title: Six and seven dimensional extrema of Non-SUSY heterotic theory with non-maximal enhancements
papers.abstract: We propose a construction of non-supersymmetric heterotic theories on $T^n$ for $n=1,2,3,4$ that lead to extrema of the one-loop effective potential. In contrast to other approaches, we do not impose maximal gauge enhancement, instead relying on Weyl symmetries of the right-moving part of the momentum lattice to ensure that we get an extremum. The classification depends on finding all lattices within a given genus using Kneser's method. We find several thousand extrema, most of which have non-maximal rank gauge enhancements. Several hundred of our extrema are tachyon-free, and several dozen are also not knife edges. There may be further equivalences among these points, but we find at least 2, 11, and 38 distinct tachyon-free non-knife-edge points for $T^2$, $T^3$, and $T^4$, respectively. In addition, we build on our previous work to study the perturbative stability of $AdS_{3}\times S^{3}\times T^{4}$ backgrounds by calculating the Hessian at the extrema in the $T^4$ moduli space. The lowest eigenvalues of the Hessian at all of these $ADE$ points show violations of the BF bound and satisfy the refined deSitter conjecture.
authors: Stevell Muller, Daniel Robbins, Hassaan Saleem

papers.title: Universal and nonuniversal pole-skipping points
papers.abstract: We study the pole-skipping phenomenon for a holographic superfluid/superconductor near the critical point using dual analytic Green's functions (arXiv:2605.20415 [hep-th]). (1) There is a hydrodynamic pole-skipping point that is common to all Green's functions: this point was obtained from the near-horizon analysis previously. (2) In addition, if one examines each Green's functions, the Green's functions have additional pole-skipping points. Unlike the conventional pole-skipping points, they do not satisfy the universality, i.e., they are not located at $\omega=-(2\pi T)ni$, where $n$ is an integer. (3) We also point out that a pole-skipping does not necessary implies an ambiguity of a Green's function.
authors: Makoto Natsuume

papers.title: Soft scalar-field corrections to the topological susceptibility
papers.abstract: We compute the contribution from soft scalar-field fluctuations to the topological susceptibility in SU(2) gauge theory at high temperature. We construct a 3-dimensional effective theory for the scalar field that accounts for the presence of an instanton. In the limit that the scalar selfcoupling $ \lambda $ is much larger than the square of the gauge coupling $g$ we obtain a correction of order $\sqrt{\lambda}$ relative to the 1-loop result for the topological susceptibility.
authors: Dietrich Bodeker, Rasmus S. K. Nielsen

papers.title: Discontinuity at the Pole
papers.abstract: The exchange of a particle whose mass is taken to zero need not reproduce the exchange of a particle that is strictly massless from the outset. We derive a general on-shell diagnostic of the well-known discontinuity between the exchange of a massless particle and the massless limit of a massive-particle exchange, valid for a mediator of arbitrary integer spin S. Our main observation is that this discontinuity can be identified directly at the level of the pole residue. We find that, in four dimensions, the residue is governed by a Chebyshev polynomial in the massless case and by a Legendre polynomial in the massless limit of the massive case. For S = 2, this reproduces the van Dam-Veltman-Zakharov discontinuity. For general S, it provides a simple and compact higher-spin analogue from on-shell factorisation. The discontinuity is probed, in principle, by the leading post-Newtonian correction to the non-relativistic potential between two massive scalar bodies.
authors: Dominik Haslehner, Elena Kaiser, Javi Serra, Andreas Weiler

papers.title: Generalized Thermodynamics and Phase Transitions of Vaidya-adS Black Holes
papers.abstract: This work investigates the thermodynamics of non-stationary anti-de Sitter (adS) black holes and their gauge-gravity duals. To model a non-equilibrium process, we employ a time-dependent Vaidya-adS metric to describe the collapse of a null fluid and the subsequent thermalization of the dual field theory. We introduce an effective version of free energy as a quasilocal probe to be used in a dynamical setup. By analyzing how this quantity evolves, we show that a first-order phase transition occurs when the final black-hole mass exceeds the limit established by the Hawking-Page temperature. Furthermore, we demonstrate that the final state only approaches the thermal behavior of the N=4 supersymmetric Yang-Mills theory for mass states much larger than the adS radius. Finally, we compute the boundary energy-momentum tensor using holographic renormalization and compare the resulting energy density with the strong-coupling limit. This demonstrates that the dual description provides a consistent framework for both the equilibrium and non-equilibrium thermodynamics of strongly coupled gauge theories.
authors: A. F. Cardona, C. Molina

papers.title: Prospects of Detecting Cosmological Domain Walls in the Cosmic Microwave Background
papers.abstract: Topological defects are a generic prediction of field theories with spontaneously broken symmetries, and domain walls, the two-dimensional defects left by a broken discrete symmetry, are among the simplest. We study the imprint of dark, purely gravitationally interacting domain walls on the Cosmic Microwave Background (CMB), in the regime where a low symmetry-breaking scale $\eta$ allows the walls to evade the Zel'dovich overclosure bound while remaining cosmologically relevant. The relativistic repulsion of matter by a planar wall carves out an evacuated void bounded by an overdense shell, and we compute the resulting photon deflection field analytically for walls both aligned with and arbitrarily inclined to the line of sight. The deflection stamps coherent, strongly non-Gaussian distortions onto the temperature sky, with a characteristic two-peak structure set by the relativistic displacement scale and an inclination dependence that vanishes for face-on walls. Because these signatures are localised and anisotropic, they are poorly captured by two-point statistics; we therefore analyse them with a curvelet/wavelet decomposition matched to the wall's geometry, and with simulation-based inference, training a Neural Posterior Estimator (NPE) to recover the scattering redshift $z$, energy scale $\eta$, and inclination $\theta$, and a Neural Ratio Estimator (NRE) to evaluate the likelihood-ratio test statistic for limit-setting. Casting these methods as sensitivity forecasts for a South Pole Telescope-like (SPT) survey, we find that the curvelet and wavelet statistical thresholds populate a common $\eta \sim 10-100$ MeV band over the accessible redshift range. The neural-ratio sensitivity curve, which exploits the full map morphology, reaches a factor 1.3-1.9 lower in $\eta$ at $z \gtrsim 20$, or $\sim 2-7$ in the wall tension, landing essentially on the per-resolution-element noise floor.
authors: Berkin G\"urb\"uz, Robert Brandenberger, Yitian Sun

papers.title: The Entire Quantum Computer on a Classical Leash
papers.abstract: We show that a classical client with no quantum hardware can use a single untrusted and potentially malicious quantum server as if it were its own trusted quantum computer. Through the server, the client can privately choose and run quantum computations, prepare quantum states, and process quantum states supplied by other parties. It can also keep quantum memory on the server, hidden from the server itself, and use that memory in later computations so its quantum state persists across rounds of interaction. Together, these capabilities let a purely classical party act as a quantum party in a variety of interactive protocols. We expect this virtual quantum computer to be a broadly useful tool. As immediate applications, we resolve two known open problems: (1) classical verification of quantum sampling with negligible computational soundness error, and (2) remote state preparation of arbitrary efficiently preparable quantum states. Underlying all of these results is a general-purpose, maliciously secure two-party computation protocol between a classical client and a quantum server, which we construct assuming only the post-quantum hardness of learning with errors.
authors: Yael Tauman Kalai, Dakshita Khurana, Justin Raizes

papers.title: Minkowski metric signature as a statistical prediction of piecewise-flat quantum gravity
papers.abstract: We study an ab initio calculation of the signature of the spacetime metric, within the framework of piecewise-flat models of quantum gravity. Applying numerical techniques, we evaluate the probability that any 4-simplex in a triangulation of a spacetime manifold has a given metric signature. For this we use a toy-model of quantum gravity based on quantum Regge calculus, where we ignore any effects due to dynamics and focus only on the kinematics of the configuration space. Our results may hold even for other QG models, as long as they behave similarly in the same approximation. We obtain that for a suitably chosen spacelike domain of edge lengths and the UV cutoff, the probability of observing Minkowski signature reaches approximately 85%. In contrast, allowing both spacelike and timelike edge lengths leads to the split signature being dominant, with probability between 72% and 81%. The results are essentially independent of the choice of topology and triangulation of the spacetime manifold. Our findings demonstrate that the signature of the metric does not necessarily need to be postulated in a given model of quantum gravity, but can instead be predicted from it, and we estimate the relative size of the UV cutoff and the domain for edge lengths that a given model should incorporate in order to predict the Minkowski signature with high probability. There is a potential to further increase this probability by taking into account the dynamics of the theory.
authors: Mihailo Djordjevic, Igor Prlina, Marko Vojinovic

papers.title: Fermions Scattering Off Non-Abelian Rotors
papers.abstract: We study the dynamics of $d=1+1$ chiral fermions interacting with a rotor impurity. The rotors are non-Abelian, taking values in either an $SU(N)$ group manifold, or an $SU(N)/SO(N)$ coset. At low energies, the fermions pass through the impurity, seemingly unimpeded, but trailing a topological line that is necessary for current conservation. In certain cases, these topological lines exhibit non-Abelian fusion and braiding. This can be viewed as a toy model that captures aspects of s-wave monopole-fermion scattering in $d=3+1$ dimensions.
authors: George Koundouros, David Tong

papers.title: Quantum Complexity and Stabilizer-State Expansions: From Pairing to Deformation in Fermionic Systems
papers.abstract: Understanding how collective phenomena such as pairing and deformation emerge in interacting fermionic systems, and how the correlations underlying them shape the resources required for their simulation, is a central challenge in many-body physics. We investigate various aspects of quantum complexity in a fermionic system exhibiting two main forms of collectivity, specifically deformation and pairing, through entanglement, non-stabilizerness, and fermionic non-Gaussianity. In the deformed phase, high entanglement coexists with low non-stabilizerness, while the superfluid pairing phase, by contrast, exhibits substantial multipartite entanglement and non-stabilizerness, together with maximal fermionic anti-flatness. In a second step we examine how to describe the phase diagram of the system in a classically scalable and symmetry-preserving way, by combining stabilizer-state expansion and variational basis optimization. A physics-guided decomposition of the Hamiltonian identifies the relevant stabilizer states, which can be constructed from graph states. A single stabilizer state captures the deformed phase to a large extent, and, although the number of stabilizer states required to describe the pairing phase grows exponentially with system size, a symmetry-preserving basis rotation yields a high-fidelity approximation using far fewer states. This rotated state can then serve as a practical starting point for quantum refinement.
authors: S. Momme Hengstenberg, Caroline E. P. Robin

papers.title: Quasideterminants and differential realizations of W-algebras
papers.abstract: In this work, we study the Hamiltonian reduction, used in constructing finite rectangular $W$-algebras, of the big-cell differential realization of $\mathfrak{gl}_{np}$. We establish an intrinsic factorization of the reduced differential realization, identifying its Yangian action with the coproduct action on a tensor product of $n$ evaluation differential realizations of $\mathfrak{gl}_p$. Corner quasideterminants provide the essential noncommutative mechanism through which Hamiltonian reduction transforms the higher-rank differential realization into a factorized lower-rank Yangian action.
authors: Sergey Derkachov, Daniil Getta

papers.title: Photoelectrons resolve the phase-dependent variance of bright squeezed vacuum
papers.abstract: The variance of bright squeezed vacuum (BSV) is not only strong but also phase dependent, yet recent strong-field experiments with BSV have recorded only its magnitude. A coherent field of the same color provides the phase reference that resolves this phase-dependent noise. Strong-field ionization of xenon by this light shows that the photoelectron yield follows the BSV quadrature along the coherent field, and that the nonlinearity of ionization amplifies the quadrature noise many times over in the electron yield. The noise is moreover distributed unevenly over the photoelectron momentum distribution, differing by an order of magnitude between ionization channels. Strong-field ionization thus offers a phase-sensitive, channel-resolved detector of quantum light, while the quadrature noise of quantum light offers a probe of the intensity dependence of individual ionization pathways.
authors: Haoran Ma, Yihe Wang, Chuan Cheng, Ian Gabalski, Aaron M. Ghrist, Eleanor Weckwerth, Mohammed Th. Hassan, Philip H. Bucksbaum

papers.title: SILMARILS-MV: Information-Theoretically Secure Multi-Verifier Signatures with Dealer-Free Key Issuance and Linear Aggregation for Permissioned Blockchains
papers.abstract: Permissioned blockchains authenticate transactions, votes and quorum certificates with computationally secure signatures, and post-quantum replacements inflate consensus traffic by orders of magnitude. Information-theoretic alternatives have required a trusted authority, quantum channels, per-signature interaction, or single-use keys with bounded transfer. We present SILMARILS-MV, a multi-verifier unconditionally secure signature in which a signature is the vector $\alpha = A\,e(m)$ and each verifier holds a secret functional $c_i = \Gamma^T \lambda(x_i)$ derived from virtual anchors $\Gamma$ that nobody learns. Against unbounded adversaries corrupting up to $\omega$ verifiers and any signers, and observing every decision, an honest verifier accepts a forged or invalid signature with probability at most $Q/q + 1/(q-1)$, a bound that is tight in its leading term. The scheme is strongly unforgeable, non-repudiable, transferable across unboundedly many hops, and linearly aggregatable. Keys are issued by the validators through perfectly secure MPC for $t < n/3$, without broadcast. To scale, we let the committee itself sign: in threshold notarization, finality certificates have constant size $32(\omega+1)$ bytes and per-validator issuance cost no longer depends on $n$. Arbiter-verified keys give clients 32-byte signatures, robust redistribution supports membership changes and share refresh, and verifiers can be enrolled retroactively. A certificate verifies in 2.4 microseconds. In an analytic normal-case model at 1000 validators, threshold notarization needs 71 KiB of authentication traffic per validator per block, 22x less than ML-DSA-44 for admitted verifiers. In a Rust HotStuff prototype with 100 validators, SILMARILS-MV commits 2.8x more transactions per second than ML-DSA-44 with 67x less cryptographic CPU, and Monte-Carlo attacks match the bounds.
authors: Khadijeh Bagheri, Hassan Khodaiemehr, Chen Feng

papers.title: A Topology-Aware Quantum-Classical Framework for Multi-Target Active Debris Removal using Gaussian Boson Sampling
papers.abstract: The continued growth of orbital debris threatens the safety and sustainability of near-Earth space, making Active Debris Removal (ADR) an important mitigation strategy. Selecting $k$ targets from $N$ candidates yields a combinatorial search space of size $\binom{N}{k}$, making joint target selection and mission sequencing computationally demanding. We present a topology-aware quantum-classical framework integrating orbital mechanics, weighted orbital-transfer graphs, Gaussian Boson Sampling (GBS), and multi-objective evolutionary optimization. Seven target-prioritization strategies represent physical consequence, orbital persistence, conjunction risk, network centrality, community structure, inferred source families, and random selection. GBS generates candidate target subsets from the weighted graph, which are then evaluated using PyGMO-based evolutionary optimization to identify servicing sequences that jointly minimize total velocity increment ($\Delta v$) and mission duration, accounting for modeled timing, propulsion, and mass feasibility. We evaluate the framework across three benchmark environments, SOCRATES Minefield, Collision Cloud, and Random, with candidate-pool sizes $N\in\{15,18,22,25\}$ and target cardinalities $k\in\{3,5\}$. The experiments characterize how benchmark topology, prioritization strategy, and problem scale relate to sampling behavior and downstream mission performance. By separating candidate-subset generation from detailed trajectory optimization, the framework offers a topology-aware approach to focusing computational effort on a limited set of candidate ADR missions.
authors: Komal Pandya, Saiyam Sakhuja, Nagaraj Kattian

papers.title: Gauge conditions in the perturbative quantization of quadratic gravity and its quantum Lagrangian
papers.abstract: In the perturbative formulation of the Hamiltonian of quadratic gravity, a specific gauge condition is required to hold the equivalence of the Hamiltonian equations of motion with the covariant field equations. Here we give robust evidence that this is an effect of perturbations, the exact nonperturbative equations of both formulations are equivalent, with no need of specific gauge conditions. Despite this, the required gauge condition must be imposed in the perturbative approach. We use it, together with other conditions obtained on very broad grounds, to obtain the quantum Lagrangian resulting from the integration on the canonical variables of the BFV quantization of the theory. This allow us to characterize the quantum modes from the Lagrangian perspective.
authors: Jorge Bellorin, Claudio B\'orquez, Byron Droguett

papers.title: Bounded compositions and products of chains, or bi(s)nomials everywhere from de Moivre's formula to spin multiplicities and constant-sum codes
papers.abstract: How many ways are there to select $k$ objects from $n$ types when type $i$ is available in only $s_{i}$ copies? For equal bounds, this is de Moivre's problem of obtaining a prescribed total with $n$ dice, now a textbook application of the principle of inclusion-exclusion. For arbitrary bounds, the answer is encoded by the rank polynomial $\prod_{i=1}^{n}(1+x+\cdots+x^{s_{i}})$. Its coefficients enumerate bounded compositions and submultisets, give, after normalization, the probability mass function of a sum of independent discrete uniform random variables, and are the weight multiplicities of a tensor product of $\mathrm{SU}(2)$ representations. Most of these interpretations are classical but dispersed; here we place them in a common notation and document their provenance. A complement involution proves symmetry and boundary identities. For arbitrary bounds, lower-half first differences give both symmetric-chain starts and mixed-spin multiplicities, and the chain-length and irreducible-dimension profiles agree. Convolution gives log-concavity and the central mode. For equal bounds with fixed $s \geq 1$ and even $ns$, local expansions give central asymptotics with explicit $1/n$ and $1/n^{2}$ corrections for the coefficient and its first difference. A Poisson limit gives the first boundary crossover of these differences at scale $k \sim \lambda n^{s/(s+1)}$, with factor $e^{-\alpha\lambda^{s+1}}$ when the proportion of bounds equal to the fixed minimum $s \geq 1$ tends to $\alpha>0$. Central first differences include the $s$-Catalan numbers, themselves Littlewood-Richardson coefficients; central layers yield maximum-size constant-sum codebooks for hash-based signatures. Under the polynomial binomial convention, the full inclusion-exclusion transform vanishes, and the omitted terms sum to the negative of the number of bounded compositions.
authors: Hac\`{e}ne Belbachir, Jos\'{e} Ricardo G. Mendon\c{c}a

papers.title: A generalization of Gordon's Theorem to arbitrary winding number
papers.abstract: We study minimizers of the Keplerian action functional with homogeneous potential of type $1/|u|^\alpha$ on periodic loops with fixed winding number $k \in \mathbb{Z}\setminus\{0\}$. This extends the classical theorems of Gordon and Venturelli, closing the previously open case $\alpha \in (1,2)$, $|k|\geq 2$. We show that the $k$-circular solution loses local minimality below the threshold $\alpha = 2-1/|k|^2$, and that minimizers are collision-free above $\alpha = 2-1/|k|$. Combining these results with the existence of precessing periodic orbits in between, we obtain a full classification of the minimizer in terms of $\alpha$ and $k$, which we also verify numerically for $k=2$.
authors: M. Fenucci

papers.title: Temporal Degeneracy Limits Message Passing Decoding of QLDPC Codes Under Repeated Noisy Syndrome Measurements
papers.abstract: Practical quantum computations can require logical error rates of $10^{-12}$ or lower. Quantum low-density parity-check (QLDPC) codes are promising candidates for reaching such rates with low qubit overhead, provided that their syndromes can be decoded efficiently. Repeated noisy syndrome measurements introduce temporal degeneracy into the space-time decoding graph. We characterize the temporal kernel, whose vectors have zero total data parity, and show that it is generated by elementary temporal codewords of weight $d_v+2$, where $d_v$ is the variable-node degree. For $(d_v,d_c)$-regular parity-check matrices with fixed degrees $d_v,d_c>2$ and girth greater than four, we derive counting bounds and construct degenerate error patterns of weight $(d_v+2)/2$ for even $d_v$ and $d_v+1$ for odd $d_v$, with multiplicity $\Theta(nr)$ in the blocklength $n$ and number of measurement rounds $r$. Under the isolation assumption, these patterns cause local failures of deterministic isotropic message-passing decoders under a flooding schedule. These failures depend on the node degrees rather than the minimum distance; for the bivariate bicycle (BB) codes considered, their weight is equal to four. Monte carlo simulations and fixed-weight importance sampling quantify harmful low-weight degenerate error patterns for the min-sum (MS) decoder beyond the isolation assumption. Motivated by the identified symmetries, we propose space-time anisotropic min-sum decoding with syndrome-guided realizations. Its complexity is linear in the number of Tanner graph edges for fixed maximum number of iterations and number of decoders. Numerical results on BB codes show threshold-like behavior acrossthe tested code sizes and improved failure probabilities relative to MS decoding with ordered statistics decoding post-processing.
authors: Dimitris Chytas, Nithin Raveendran, Bane Vasi\'{c}

papers.title: Optimal Control of a Fluxonium Circuit with the Q-PRONTO Numerical Method
papers.abstract: Optimizing the control of large quantum systems is a resource-intensive task, where the convergence rate of the underlying iterative schemes is crucial. The recently developed Quantum Projection Operator-Based Newton Method for Trajectory Optimization (Q-PRONTO) offers a unique quadratic convergence for controlling quantum states, while most model-based solvers guarantee only an approximately linear convergence rate. As a proof of concept, here, we design and benchmark single-qubit gates optimized by Q-PRONTO based on the circuit Hamiltonian of a fluxonium superconducting qubit. To ensure that we can apply a long string of arbitrary pulses to the circuit, we modify the firmware associated with the Quantum Instrumentation Control Kit (QICK) by altering its memory allocation. We characterize the performance of the optimal solutions using standard randomized benchmarking and achieve a total error per gate of $6.6\times10^{-4}$.
authors: John Barta, Brian D. Isakov, Pablo Aramburu Sanchez, Jieqiu Shao, Tam\'as Kalm\'ar, Trevyn F. Q. Larson, Marco M. Nicotra, Andr\'as Gyenis

papers.title: Graphical Rigidity of Continuous Variable Graph States under Gaussian Local Transformations
papers.abstract: Multimode entangled pure Gaussian states are an essential resource for continuous variable (CV) quantum information processing. Menicucci et al. [2011] have shown how to describe them as graphs with complex adjacency matrices. Among such complex graph states (CGSs), quantum optics experimental setups straightforwardly display correlations described by purely imaginary graph states (iRGSs) whereas theoretical literature favors off-diagonal real graph state (RGS) descriptions, which actually reflect the entanglement structure in the infinite squeezing limit [Gonzalez-Arciniegas et al. 2021]. We study them beyond this ideal case, thus establishing in the finite squeezing regime an equivalence criterion for the generic case of CGSs through a graph propagating set of conditions which either finds a Gaussian Local Unitary (GLU) converting one state to another or gives a proof of impossibility if such a GLU does not exist. In the experimentally relevant case of the conversion between iRGSs and RGSs, the set of conditions results in simple relations between the topologies of the equivalent real and imaginary graphs. Finally, we show that the canonical forms of iRGSs and RGSs imply that the topology of the CV real and imaginary graph states are too rigid to admit any exact qumode local-addition analogue to the qubit complementation or qudit local-addition, thus demonstrating the non-existence of any exact qumode local-addition for these states. We however define an approximate one when the squeezing is strong enough.
authors: Giorgio Ciliberto, Fr\'ed\'eric Grosshans

papers.title: Fidelity Dynamics of a Jaynes--Cummings Qubit under Markovian and Non-Markovian Coupling Noise
papers.abstract: We analytically investigate the fidelity dynamics of a Jaynes--Cummings qubit coupled to a single-mode cavity in the presence of stochastic fluctuations of the qubit--cavity coupling. Such fluctuations naturally arise in cavity- and circuit-QED platforms due to fabrication imperfections, control-field noise, mechanical vibrations, and environmental disturbances. Since the qubit--cavity coupling governs the rate of coherent energy and information exchange, understanding the effects of its fluctuations is essential for assessing the performance of quantum communication, quantum sensing, and quantum information-processing protocols. We consider both Gaussian white noise and Ornstein--Uhlenbeck noise with finite correlation time as models for the coupling fluctuations. Exploiting the closed dynamics within each excitation manifold, we derive exact analytical expressions for the noise-averaged density matrix and the fidelity relative to the ideal noiseless evolution. We show that the fidelity is determined by a single decoherence factor governed by the integrated noise correlation function, establishing a direct connection between microscopic coupling fluctuations and macroscopic coherence loss. In the white-noise limit, the fidelity decays exponentially, whereas finite noise correlation times produce nonexponential decay and slower coherence loss. We further show that the crossover between Markovian-like and non-Markovian regimes is controlled by the ratio of the noise correlation rate to the coherent coupling strength, and that decoherence increases with photon number because of the enhanced effective qubit--cavity coupling. These results provide a unified analytical framework for quantifying decoherence induced by stochastic coupling fluctuations and for evaluating the robustness of cavity-QED protocols under correlated noise.
authors: Fang Wang, Da-Wei Luo, Ting Yu

papers.title: Probabilistic representation and Monte Carlo method for nonlinear Dirac equations
papers.abstract: Dirac equations describe the relativistic evolution of quantum particles. Using the point-process stochastic calculus of piecewise-deterministic Markov processes (PDMPs) on general state spaces, which naturally allows additional Feynman-Kac potentials, we develop a probabilistic representation for the nonlinear Dirac equations in $1+1$ spacetime dimension with cubic nonlinearity and $L_\infty$-type problem data using a multi-type branching telegraph process together with both continuous and jump-type multiplicative functionals. Our main theorem leads to a classification result which, when applied to the specific Soler model, gives a sharp finite-time admissibility of the probabilistic representation. By extending the one-step representation to a multi-step, time-marching representation using an analytically-derived a priori $L_\infty$ estimate, we observe a ``local probabilistic representation, but global PDE well-posedness" phenomenon. We proceed to propose a time-marching Monte Carlo algorithm as a global numerical solver for the Soler system with a rigorous convergence proof and establish an additional stability result on the PDE side. Finally, while the underlying process parameters do not affect the validity of the probabilistic representation, we observe their potential for variance reduction in the Monte Carlo methods.
authors: Jean-Pierre Fouque, Tomoyuki Ichiba, Ka Lok Lam

papers.title: Noise-Assisted Quantum Entanglement: Memory-Enhanced Coherence in Stochastic Jaynes-Cummings Dynamics
papers.abstract: We investigate qubit entanglement dynamics in a two-qubit cavity system with stochastically fluctuating coupling strength, comparing white noise (Markovian) and Ornstein-Uhlenbeck noise (non-Markovian) processes. We analytically solve the system dynamics for both Fock and coherent cavity states and systematically characterize how initial qubit configurations affect entanglement generation and preservation. Our results reveal distinct dynamical regimes: in the Fock-state cavity, initial states in the single-excitation subspace generate robust qubit entanglement in decoherence-free subspaces, while initially entangled states in the double-excitation subspace exhibit inevitable decay without protective symmetries. For coherent cavities, we identify a critical photon-number threshold in the intermediate coherent-state amplitude regime where dynamics transition from low-frequency to high-frequency entanglement oscillations, while universal entanglement loss occurs at large amplitudes. Remarkable resilience against entanglement sudden death emerges under strong non-Markovian noise with long correlation times, where repeated revivals occur. These findings establish cavity photon statistics and environmental memory time as key control parameters for engineering qubit entanglement dynamics in qubit-cavity systems, revealing how system-environment correlations govern quantum information preservation.
authors: Fang Wang, Quanzhen Ding, Jun Jing, Ting Yu

papers.title: Towards ${\cal N}=8$ Supergravity in ${\cal N}=1$ Superspace
papers.abstract: We study the possibility of constructing maximally supersymmetric supergravity in ${\cal N}=1$ superspace. We dimensionally reduce the eleven dimensional supersymmetry transformations, and decouple these transformations using the residual $G_2$ symmetry of the theory. This allows us to find the ${\cal N}=1$ superfields relevant to this theory. Among our results, we find a description of a self-dual superfield involving a spin 1 and a spin 3/2 field which does not seem to have been discussed previously in the literature.
authors: Arvind Rajaraman

papers.title: Melonic ladder holography with a single free bulk field in AdS$_{d+1}$
papers.abstract: We derive a cylinder from the pair Casimir of a CFT$_d$: at zero centre momentum it depends only on relative dilations and rotations. Relative-coordinate radial quantisation then encodes exchanged family labels as cylinder energies. For a melonic CFT$_d$ in the normalisable and stable range, the reduced ladder sum is the Robin boundary-to-boundary propagator of a single free scalar field in rigid AdS$_{d+1}$, with the cylinder as its conformal boundary. The Robin boundary condition and bulk regularity (or parity) determine the holographic radial extension of the boundary data. A nonzero Robin boundary coefficient in global AdS breaks $2d$ AdS generators, yet the scalar's boundary propagator still encodes the conformal data of the melonic ladder. We demonstrate the correspondence for the Sachdev--Ye--Kitaev and the $d=2$ disorder-free long-range Amit--Roginsky melonic models, which correspond to a single free local scalar in AdS$_2$ and AdS$_3$, respectively.
authors: Kok Hong Thong

papers.title: Demonstrating RFSoC-based Control of a Fully Connected Exchange-Only Qubit
papers.abstract: Semiconductor triple-quantum dots (TQDs) are a promising platform for scalable quantum information processing, but the community has so far lacked access to affordable and flexible high-speed control electronics. SpinQICK, an open-source spin qubit-control package built on the Xilinx Radio Frequency System-on-Chip (RFSoC), directly addresses this gap by leveraging the high sampling-rate signal generation and advanced digital signal processing (DSP) capabilities of the Quantum Instrumentation Control Kit (QICK) to enable precise time-domain voltage control and readout of semiconductor spin qubits. In this paper, we use spinQICK to demonstrate coherent control, state preparation, and readout of a fully connected triangular exchange-only device. We also introduce and experimentally verify a novel dynamical decoupling (DD) sequence enabled by the triangular TQD and leverage its unique decoupling properties to characterize electrical noise. These results establish spinQICK as a low-cost, flexible platform for semiconductor spin qubit control and provide a pathway for hardware optimization through qubit-level noise diagnostics.
authors: Abigail L. Wessels, M. Garrett Bimstefer, Joseph D. Broz, Alen Senanian, Andrew E. Oriani

papers.title: QuantumMatterExplorer: An Autonomous Agent for the Discovery of Quantum Many-Body Phases of Matter
papers.abstract: Mapping the phase diagram of a new quantum Hamiltonian demands expert judgement at every step: which observables to measure, where in parameter space to compute, or how to separate genuine order from finite-size artefacts. We introduce QuantumMatterExplorer, an autonomous agent that takes only a Hamiltonian and its parameter ranges as input and returns a phase diagram obtained from its own numerical simulations. The agent is built on a large language model and is designed to reason over a long horizon, maintain a persistent written plan, and drive a set of computational tools, with density-matrix renormalization group (DMRG) calculations cross-checked against independent exact diagonalization. The agent combines a large language model with persistent planning, a library of expert computational-physics skills, and density-matrix renormalization group calculations validated against independent exact diagonalization. It adaptively selects quantities to evaluate, refines parameter scans, and performs finite-size analyses as evidence accumulates. After validating the approach on Hamiltonians with known transitions, we challenge it with a frustrated bilinear-biquadratic spin-1 chain with single-ion anisotropy, whose two-dimensional phase diagram was published only recently and is unlikely to appear in any training corpus. Given no hint about the expected physics, the agent proposes which observables to probe, and identifies candidate N\'eel, Haldane and dimerized phases, in broad agreement with the reference phase diagram. It also detects incommensurate correlations and infers the frustration-dependent geometry of the phase boundaries, all within an eight-hour compute budget. These results open a practical route to the autonomous computational discovery of new phases of quantum matter.
authors: Jannes Nys, Andrew Jreissaty, Juan Carrasquilla

papers.title: Additive uncertainty relations via pseudospectral methods
papers.abstract: Given Hermitian observable $A$, the variance of $A$ is given by the difference of expectations $\langle A^2\rangle - \langle A\rangle^2$, where the expectation of an observable implicitly assumes a choice of state for the underlying system. As a sub-case of a general lower bound for the sum of variances for finitely many arbitrary elements in a $C^*$-algebra, we prove that the sum of the variances for $d$ observables $A_1, \dots , A_d$ is greater than some expression in the expectations $\langle i[A_j,A_k]\rangle$ for $j\neq k$ plus the square of the smallest singular value of the associated localizer. In special cases, this expression is just a root mean square average. Our technique also derives a general containment between the Clifford pseudospectra and quadratic pseudospectra for $d$ observables.
authors: Alexander Cerjan, Lara Ismert, Terry A. Loring

papers.title: Can Spontaneous Time-Translation Symmetry Breaking Be Quantized Without Explicit Branches?
papers.abstract: Can classically branched dynamics associated with spontaneous time-translation-symmetry breaking be quantized without explicitly retaining the branches of the Hamiltonian? We investigate this question using a reduced phase space. formulation in which the Hamiltonian is single-valued, while the critical structure of the classical Legendre map is encoded in a singular, momentum-dependent symplectic geometry. Quantization of the reduced Poisson algebra yields a deformed position-momentum commutator whose singularities determine distinct regular momentum sectors. Using the positive measure induced by the reduced symplectic structure, we identify a bounded central sector and two unbounded outer sectors. In the central sector, states with vanishing mean momentum obey a nonzero lower bound on position uncertainty, subject to the operator-domain assumptions of the representation. We further identify a possible field-theoretic connection with k-essence, where nonlinear scalar-field kinetics can produce finite-velocity degeneracies of the Legendre map. The relationship between the resulting reduced quantum description and branch-matching quantization remains unresolved and requires a comparison of the corresponding Hilbert spaces and operator domains.
authors: Partha Nandi

papers.title: Asymptotic scars arising from the remnants of quantum phase transitions
papers.abstract: Many-body localisation, Hilbert space fragmentation and quantum many-body scars (QMBS) are well-established mechanisms of ergodicity breaking in quantum systems. Recently, asymptotic quantum many-body scars (AQMBS), non-thermal states whose stability grows with system size, have been proposed theoretically and probed experimentally. Here, we show that AQMBS arise naturally as remnants of certain quantum phase transitions. For a broad class of frustration-free Hamiltonians, we prove that their gapless excitations survive deformation into a scarred Hamiltonian as states whose energy variance is bounded by the excitation gap. Consequently, the gapless excitations at a quantum critical point become AQMBS of the scarred Hamiltonian. Their fidelity relaxation time is then set by the critical scaling of the gap, determined by the dynamic critical exponent. Modelling the critical Fredkin and Motzkin chains and the two-dimensional PVBS model, we obtain AQMBS whose variances directly reflect the dynamic exponents of the underlying transitions. Where the gap of the Motzkin chain closes super-exponentially, we find exponentially stable AQMBS, for which we also observe numerical evidence of volume-law entanglement.
authors: Leonard Logari\'c, Shane Dooley, Tsuyoshi Okubo, Nobuyuki Yoshioka

papers.title: Robustness of Quantum Correlations and Controlled Teleportation Fidelity under Noisy Channels
papers.abstract: In distributed quantum computing, quantum networks provide a potential infrastructure for long-range quantum information processing. Controlled quantum teleportation (CQT) is a key practically relevant protocol that can connect two parties on a network and enables a third party, the controller to allow or abort the secure teleportation of an arbitrary single-qubit state between the two parties. We investigate the robustness of a three-qubit GHZ resource under bit-flip, phase-flip, depolarizing, and amplitude-damping noise. Using the Kraus-operator formalism, we characterize the noisy resource through multipartite quantum discord, genuine multipartite concurrence (GMC), localizable entanglement (LE), and CQT fidelity. We also outline a proof-of-concept photonic implementation for preparing the three-qubit GHZ resource and realizing the CQT protocol, which could enable experimental investigation of the effects of noise. Our results show that bit-flip and amplitude-damping noise generally preserve useful mutipartite quantum correlations over broader noise parameter ranges. Interestingly, multipartite discord exhibits freezing under bit-flip noise over a finite parameter regime. Moreover, discord can persist beyond the sudden death of genuine multipartite entanglement, revealing the distinct robustness of nonclassical correlations. We further demonstrate that CQT fidelity which characterizes the performance of CQT can exceed the classical threshold even after GMC vanishes, while LE more closely reflects the operational usefulness of the noisy resource. These findings highlight the complementary roles of quantum correlations and entanglement in assessing the resilience of GHZ-based protocols.
authors: S. Archana, Aditi Das, Venkat Abhignan, R. Muthuganesan

papers.title: Real-space construction and selection rules of center-of-mass momentum eigenstates in two-dimensional many-body lattices
papers.abstract: We present a comprehensive framework for the real-space construction of center-of-mass (c.m.) momentum eigenstates in two-dimensional (2D) quantum many-body systems. Unlike standard momentum-space approaches, our real-space formalism explicitly captures the non-uniformity of cyclic subspace dimensions, which are fundamentally governed by the spatial symmetries of the many-body configurations and particle statistics. We demonstrate that performing 2D real-space translations on multi-particle states naturally induces non-trivial translation phase factors associated with the characters of these stabilizer subgroups, leading to a renormalization of permissible momentum values. Notably, we identify an anomalous cross-dimensional momentum coupling in highly symmetric particle distributions, where the permissible momentum values in one direction are strictly constrained by those in the perpendicular direction. We emphasize the algorithmic necessity of this coupling, as neglecting it leads to missing or duplicated basis states in numerical implementations. Concrete examples are provided to demonstrate the practical implementation and physical consequences of this framework.
authors: Ling Lin, Yongguan Ke, Chaohong Lee

papers.title: Material criteria for angular-momentum transfer from twisted photons to photoelectrons
papers.abstract: We study the material requirements for transferring the total-angular-momentum (TAM) projection of a twisted photon to the orbital angular momentum (OAM) of a photoelectron emitted from an $n$-type semiconductor surface. Within a single-valley effective-mass model of surface photoemission, we calculate OAM-resolved spectra for GaAs, InSb, $\mathrm{InAs}_{0.34}\mathrm{Sb}_{0.66}$, and $\mathrm{Hg}_{0.76}\mathrm{Cd}_{0.24}\mathrm{Te}$ irradiated by twisted photons with Laguerre--Gaussian--like momentum profile. The OAM transfer is characterized by the mean electron OAM, its root-mean-squared width, and the fraction of electrons with OAM-projection equal to the photon TAM-projection. Efficient transfer requires the transverse momentum of the conduction electron to be much smaller than the transverse momentum width of the photon, which favors low temperatures, small conduction-band effective masses, and shallow donor levels. GaAs is less favorable within the present model because of its larger effective mass and deeper donor levels. We also discuss the demanding photon-wave packet parameters, possible extensions to Dirac and Weyl semimetals, and post-emission OAM selection. Although the generation of vortex electrons with a vanishing OAM uncertainty via photoemission seems challenging, we argue that it is still possible to generate single-electron vortex states with a finite OAM dispersion.
authors: A. A. Shchepkin, D. V. Karlovets

papers.title: Kinetic competition controls loss-induced exceptional points of Hubbard pairs
papers.abstract: Two-body loss can bind two fermions in a Hubbard lattice, yet the binding threshold in the infinite lattice need not be an exceptional point (EP). At fixed total momentum $\mathbf{K}$, the hops of the two particles interfere into a relative-motion hopping along each lattice direction, which sets the kinetic energy of the relative motion. On a hypercubic lattice, the threshold $g_c=1/[\pi\rho_2(0)]$ is an EP precisely when the maximum kinetic energy along one direction exceeds the sum of the transverse maxima. This dominance keeps every transverse-momentum scattering channel propagating near the band center, making the local pair Green function purely imaginary there. Two real-energy scattering zeros associated with coherent perfect absorption then coalesce at the threshold into a second-order EP of the analytically continued pair problem, where loss restores the parity-time symmetry of the pair's scattering solutions. Without a dominant direction, binding occurs without coalescence and without breaking of that symmetry. Total momentum can therefore select EP sectors even on isotropic lattices. More broadly, the kinetic structure of the two-particle continuum determines whether loss-induced binding and exceptional degeneracy coincide.
authors: Ho-Kin Tang, Xiaosen Yang

papers.title: Quantum Cryptomania with Classical Communication without One-Way Functions
papers.abstract: In classical cryptography, one-way functions are necessary for most of cryptography. In the quantum world, however, Kretschmer at {TQC'21} and subsequent works have demonstrated that quantum versions of various primitives in minicrypt, such as signatures and private-key encryption, do not require quantum-computable one-way functions (\textsf{qOWF}s). However, the question of the necessity of \textsf{qOWF}s for primitives in Cryptomania like public-key encryption with classical public keys and ciphertexts (\textsf{qPKE}) has remained open. We provide a comprehensive picture of the relationship between \textsf{qPKE} and \textsf{qOWF}. First, our main result is a black-box separation between \textsf{qOWF}s and \textsf{qPKE}. In particular, we show that relative to a unitary, real, and self-inverse oracle, there exists a \textsf{qPKE} scheme (with classical keys and ciphertexts), but \textsf{qOWF}s do not exist. Further, our oracles admit a point-function obfuscation construction, thus ruling out black-box construction of \textsf{qOWF} from point function obfuscations. On the positive side, we construct \textsf{qPKE} from quantum indistinguishability obfuscation for quantum circuits with classical obfuscated descriptions and efficiently verifiable one-way puzzles, which is known to be a potentially weaker assumption than \textsf{qOWF}s, due to an existing black-box separation. Our construction is the quantum analog of the classical construction of \textsf{PKE} from one-way functions and indistinguishability obfuscation in the quantum computation with classical communication (QCCC) setting.
authors: Mohammed Barhoush, Amit Behera

papers.title: Spin Toda systems and N-point spherical Whittaker functions
papers.abstract: We define and study a spin version of the open Toda integrable system, using the Iwasawa decomposition of a connected split real Lie group. We study spherical Whittaker functions as solutions of the spin Toda system. We also construct their N-point version and find the corresponding factorisation of the Casimir element, which yields asymptotic boundary KZB type equations.
authors: Haoyi Li

papers.title: Trident: Efficient Load Verification for Yoked Surface Codes using a Three-Level Memory Hierarchy
papers.abstract: Fault-Tolerant Quantum Computers (FTQCs) commonly use the surface code to encode program qubits as error-corrected logical qubits. Unfortunately, the surface code has a poor encoding rate, so recent work has proposed Yoked Surface Codes (YSCs), which concatenate the surface code with a high-rate quantum code. The surface code qubits in YSCs are protected by the checks, or yokes, of the high-rate code. YSCs have 1D and 2D variants, which are $1.8\times$ and $4.5\times$ more efficient than the surface code, respectively. Modern FTQC architectures use a two-level hierarchy: surface codes perform logical operations (compute) while 2D YSCs store idle program qubits (memory). To load a qubit from memory, the FTQC first performs retrieval, which logically moves a program qubit from a 2D YSC into a surface code (8 cycles). However, retrieval is not fault-tolerant, so the FTQC must verify the load by measuring all the yokes of the 2D YSC (178 cycles). As verification dominates memory access latency, eliminating it can provide a speedup of $5.7\times$. Our goal is to reduce the verification overhead of 2D YSCs while retaining their storage efficiency. We exploit the fact that 1D YSCs, though less storage-efficient, incur negligible verification latency. We propose Trident, which expands the two-level hierarchy into a three-level hierarchy by adding a small intermediate level containing a 1D YSC (L1). If most loads hit L1 rather than L2 (2D YSC tier), it can significantly reduce verification overhead. We present two variants: Trident-D (demand-driven) and Trident-P (prefetch-driven), which achieve speedups of $2.8\times$ and $4.2\times$, respectively, while increasing the physical qubit cost of memory by only 4.9%.
authors: Gunagya Singh Mamak, Suhas Vittal, Kabir Dubey, Kaitlin N. Smith, Moinuddin K. Qureshi

papers.title: Photon-Number Discrimination from Increasing Time-of-Arrival Separation in Wide Superconducting Microstrip Single-Photon Detectors
papers.abstract: Measurements of photon-number-dependent time-of-arrival (TOA) distributions in wide NbN superconducting microstrip single-photon detectors (SMSPDs) are presented. Two \SI{10}{\um}-long devices with widths of \SI{3.2}{\um} and \SI{6.4}{\um} are characterized under pulsed \SI{515}{nm} excitation. The TOA histograms are described by sums of exponentially modified Gaussian (EMG) components, with the wider device exhibiting components assigned to photon numbers up to \(n=8\). Adjacent TOA peaks become more distinguishable relative to their widths at higher photon number, in contrast to the compression of neighboring photon-number timing shifts observed in conventional narrow-wire SNSPDs. For the components assigned to \(n=7\) and \(n=8\), the FWHM-normalized peak separation is \(2.15\), and the fitted EMG distributions yield an equal-prior pairwise TOA-assignment fidelity of \(99.6\%\). The EMG exponential-tail parameter \(\tau_n\) decreases strongly with photon number, while the Gaussian-location parameter \(\mu_n\) continues to shift between neighboring components. A phenomenological model motivated by absorption-site-dependent vortex processes and collective current redistribution captures these timing trends. These results support wide SMSPDs as a platform for TOA-based photon-number discrimination at high photon number, relevant to multiphoton-state characterization and photonic quantum information processing. The same geometry also provides a setting to examine how the spatial distribution of photon absorption affects vortex-assisted detection.
authors: Hsin-Yeh Wu, Shu-Xiao Liu, Boris Tuchming, Xavier-Fran\c{c}ois Navick, Pu-Kai Wang, Yi-Ren Wu, Jia-Wern Chen, Marc Besan\c{c}on, Jean-Fran\c{c}ois Glicenstein, Pisin Chen, Yu-Jung Lu, Stathes Paganis

papers.title: Quantum Evolution Networks Learn Long-Time Coherent Dynamics in Driven Spin Registers
papers.abstract: Predicting and controlling driven quantum systems requires access to dynamics across physical parameters, initial states, and evolution times. A reusable neural model must capture this dependence while preserving unitary structure and maintaining accuracy over long-time coherent evolution. Here we introduce Quantum Evolution Networks (QENs), which map physical parameters and time to complete propagators for periodically driven three-spin registers. Shared networks learn unitary one-period propagators and compatible within-period paths, enabling predictions through known periodic composition without query-specific numerical integration. For transverse driving, the fifth-percentile fidelity, minimized over input states and sampled times, is 0.9947 over 24 periods on 256 held-out configurations. A leading-order analysis of spectrally resolved endpoint residuals predicts multicycle process error more accurately than quadratic or spectrum-averaged estimates. Interventions at matched single-period infidelity produce orders-of-magnitude differences in multicycle infidelity, demonstrating the importance of residual orientation. Compatible component replacements identify how endpoint and within-period approximations limit reconstruction accuracy. These results establish a reusable neural representation of the studied propagator families and connect its learned residual structure to its observed long-time reliability.
authors: Puran Li, Condon Lau, Xiu-Hao Deng

papers.title: Single-step SU(3) Hahn Echo in a Qutrit Atom Interferometer
papers.abstract: The Hahn echo is a well-known dynamical decoupling method that refocuses the dephasing due to energy inhomogeneities of a spin-1/2 ensemble and is widely used to extend phase coherence in quantum computers and sensors. Extensions of such techniques beyond the spin-1/2 have been reported, but have mainly used SU(2) gates, limiting their scalability. Here, we generalize the Hahn echo to qutrits using single-step SU(3) gates and extend the coherence time by more than an order of magnitude. The gates are generated through optimal control theory and implemented in an ultracold atomic ensemble in free fall. A quantum process tomography procedure benchmarks the gates and yields fidelities of ~ 93%, limited mainly by state preparation and measurement errors. Due to the geometry of the laser beams, the generalized Hahn echo also realizes a three-path Mach-Zehnder atomic interferometer with two independent interferometric phase differences. Our results therefore establish SU(3) control for dynamical decoupling of qutrits and multi-path atom interferometers, with the latter opening the possibility for vector force measurements and interferometric tests of the validity of Born's rule.
authors: Chirantan Mitra, Lucas Gabardos, Fran\c{c}ois Impens, David Gu\'ery-Odelin, David Wilkowski, Chang Chi Kwong

papers.title: Bogoliubov Dynamics and Zitterbewegung in Optical Dirac Systems
papers.abstract: We develop a bosonic Bogoliubov description of Zitterbewegung in time-dependent optical-Dirac systems. Within the optical-Dirac framework, the anomalous pair-creation and pair-annihilation terms of a bosonic Bogoliubov Hamiltonian correspond to couplings between the positive- and negative-frequency sectors, whose coherence underlies the Zitterbewegung response. When the constitutive parameters vary in time, the resulting moving-frame connection generates dynamical interbranch coupling and positive--negative-frequency coherence. Under periodic modulation, this coupling becomes resonant near $\Omega\simeq2\omega_0$, leading to parametric amplification of the coherence and consequently to an enhanced Zitterbewegung motion.
authors: Lili Yang

papers.title: Traceable Quantum Secret Sharing
papers.abstract: Quantum secret sharing protects distributed quantum information against unauthorized reconstruction, yet existing schemes provide no intrinsic accountability when shares are leaked or forged. This missing capability is particularly relevant in realistic distributed settings, where compromised participants may either expose valid shares or maliciously interfere with reconstruction. Here we establish a framework for traceable quantum secret sharing under these two threat models. We introduce leakage-verifiable and traceable quantum secret sharing (LVT-QSS), which attributes leaked shares through an explicit leakage verification mechanism, and malicious-traceable and accountable quantum secret sharing (MTA-QSS), which identifies participants who submit forged shares during reconstruction. We formulate security definitions for both settings and prove that the proposed protocols satisfy the corresponding guarantees against the relevant adversaries. Numerical simulations under per-share depolarizing noise further quantify the robustness of the proposed schemes and identify verification as the dominant noise sensitive stage. These results incorporate accountability into quantum secret sharing and provide a foundation for traceable distributed quantum cryptography.
authors: Mengyan Qiao, Jian Long, Yu Li, Zhu Cao

papers.title: Performing a Quantum Subroutine Using Cluster States
papers.abstract: Quantum subroutines, like their classical counterparts, serve as essential components of larger algorithms. They can be realized using gate based architectures or measurement based quantum computation (MBQC), where computation proceeds through adaptive measurements on highly entangled cluster states. In this work, we implement a phase oracle as a reusable subroutine within the MBQC framework using experimentally feasible cluster states. Unlike prior demonstrations of Grover's algorithm in MBQC that omit explicit oracle construction, our approach provides a transparent formulation of the oracle subroutine, including its measurement patterns, byproduct correlations, density-matrix simulations, and corresponding MBQC measurement circuits.
authors: Sakibul Islam Rayhan, Karima Hassan, Md Rasedujjaman, Md Mohsinur Rahman Adnan

papers.title: Averages of traces and ratios of characteristic polynomials of random unitary matrices
papers.abstract: In this work we explore the extent to which the Ratios Theorem for averages over $U(N)$, with respect to Haar measure, of ratios of characteristic polynomials can be used to evaluate averages of traces of unitary matrices. We derive concrete expressions for all averages involving up to 4 traces, valid for any matrix size, $N$.
